sections.h2: Which offices value, bill and collect Letcher County property tax?
sections.html:
Letcher County runs its tax through a valuation office, the sheriff and the clerk. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's value. The Letcher County Sheriff sends out the bill and receives the payment. The Letcher County Clerk inherits anything still unpaid in mid-April.

The PVA sits at 156 Main Street, Suite 105, in Whitesburg, with a phone line at 606-633-2182 and a fax at 606-633-3995. Its page on the statewide PVA portal explains that ownership, like value, is frozen as of New Year's Day, so a house bought in March still shows the seller on that year's bill. A new owner who never sees a copy can phone the sheriff at 606-633-2293.

The county government site gives the sheriff's weekday hours as 8:30 to 4 and links to a web page for paying the bill. The clerk, at 606-633-2432, keeps the same hours and runs a delinquent tax section. Phone the clerk to learn when the current year's tax sale is scheduled.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Letcher County for a seller?
sections.html:
It is a mountain county where the land shapes everything, including how a house is priced and how long it sits. Letcher County is tucked into Kentucky's southeastern tip. Pine Mountain stretches 125 miles and runs down the county's center, Black Mountain tops out near 3,700 feet along the Virginia line, and national forest covers a big slice of the acreage.

The first permanent settlement dates to 1803, at the mouth of Pert Creek where Whitesburg now stands. Lawmakers created it in 1842 from pieces of three older counties, Harlan, Perry and Pike, and gave it the name of the sitting governor. Courthouse history tells the story in miniature: a log building finished in 1844, a brick one in 1898, a modern one dedicated in 1965 and remodeled in 1998. Today Whitesburg is the seat, Jenkins is the biggest city, and Fleming-Neon makes three. Blackey, Mayking, McRoberts, Millstone and Payne Gap are unincorporated.

Coal drove the boom. Before mining the county never topped 10,000 people, and by 1940 it had passed 40,000. The Scotia mine explosions of March 1976 killed 26 miners and led to the federal mine safety act the next year. More recently the July and August 2022 floods killed three people here and left others homeless. If a building was damaged, ask the PVA how that damage shows up in the assessment.

  • Letcher County Public Schools covers most addresses, with its high school in Whitesburg.
  • Jenkins Independent Schools covers the Jenkins area, with an elementary school in Burdine and a combined middle and high school.
  • US 119 climbs Pine Mountain between Jenkins and Whitesburg, and US 23 skirts the eastern edge.
  • Fishpond Lake near Jenkins, the Pioneer Horse Trail and the recreation center draw weekend visitors, and the Mountain Heritage Festival has run since 1983.

sections.h2: How inexpensive are Letcher County homes, by the federal numbers?
sections.html:
Homes here are inexpensive, mostly owner-occupied and rarely new. The federal QuickFacts table for the county shows a population that has slid while households stay fairly stable.

With so few permits, nearly every sale is a resale, and buyers compare each house against a small set of older homes. A tax bill on a $67,400 home is small in dollars, which is why a few years of neglect can feel manageable until the penalties compound.

sections.h2: When is the Letcher County bill due, and what happens after the deadline?
sections.html:
Kentucky's collection statute, KRS 134.015, sets one calendar for every county, and the sheriff here follows it. Anyone who settles the full amount by November 1 gets 2 percent off. Between early November and year end the bill is payable at face value. January adds 5 percent, and February onward adds 10 percent plus the sheriff's fee. If the state delays a county's bills, it can swap in a schedule that allows a month per stage.

Closing time on April 15 is the cliff. The sheriff passes the unpaid list along, every item turns into a certificate of delinquency, and a lien goes on record against the house. Monthly interest of one percent starts, and the clerk and county attorney each earn commissions that climb as notices go out.

The Revenue Department's own sample shows the pace of growth. A $1,000 bill reaches the clerk at $1,254 once the penalty, fee and commission are added. If it is still open after the June newspaper ad, the sample total is $1,659.90. Investors can then buy the debt at a public sale three to four and a half months after the handoff, and the lien can last eleven years whoever owns the house.

sections.h2: How can I appeal a Letcher County assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with a sit-down at the PVA's office. The appeals panel refuses any case that skipped that meeting, and the meeting must happen before or during the viewing window.

The roll opens for public viewing on May's first Monday and stays open thirteen days. Once you have held your conference, you must file with the Letcher County Clerk by the end of the workday that follows the window. The local appeals panel then sits in Whitesburg, the county seat, roughly a month later, within 25 to 35 days of the window closing.

  • Bring proof: building and land details, insurance policies, what construction cost, and listings of similar houses. An appeal with no evidence is denied.
  • A paid advocate has to be a lawyer, accountant, consultant, broker, appraiser, your own employee or a holder of a state-recognized designation, and needs your authorization in writing.
  • Audio recording is allowed, and the panel must explain any change in writing.
  • If bills were printed before the ruling and the value rises, a supplemental bill follows.

sections.h2: Can a Letcher County senior or disabled owner cut the tax bill?
sections.html:
Yes, through the homestead exemption. For assessment years 2025 and 2026 the deduction is $49,100 off a home's taxable value. A house assessed at $120,000 would be taxed as though it were worth $70,900.

The home must be the applicant's residence, and the applicant must either reach 65 during the tax year or hold a total disability rating from a federal program or a retirement system. About 22 percent of residents are past 65, so plenty of owners may qualify. Apply at the Letcher County PVA. Disabled owners under 65 generally renew every year, except service-connected veterans and people ruled permanently disabled by the Social Security Administration or the state retirement system, who document it once. A buyer cannot inherit the break, since the exemption belongs to the person.

sections.h2: What does a Letcher County seller owe at closing?
sections.html:
The bill follows the January 1 titleholder, and the settlement statement decides who reimburses whom. A common Kentucky practice is for the seller to credit the buyer for the months of ownership, with the buyer paying the full bill when it arrives.

Kentucky also charges a transfer tax under KRS 142.050: a rate of $0.50 on every $500, or fraction, of the price stated in the deed, billed to the grantor and collected by the clerk at recording. Foreclosure transfers, spouses splitting in a divorce and nominal parent-child transfers are exempt. Because delinquent tax is a lien, closing agents insist on paying it out of the proceeds. Request a payoff figure from the sheriff before closing, and ask the clerk whether any parcel has been certified as delinquent.

faqs.q: Who gets the Letcher County tax payment?
faqs.a: Send it to the Letcher County Sheriff, who answers at 606-633-2293 on weekdays from 8:30 to 4. The county website also links to an online payment page. Anything unpaid after April 15 shifts to the county clerk.

faqs.q: Is there an early-payment discount in Letcher County?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 of the tax year takes 2 percent off. After that the printed amount is due until December 31, and penalties of 5 and then 10 percent follow.

faqs.q: I bought in Letcher County and no bill came. What now?
faqs.a: Phone the sheriff at 606-633-2293 and ask for a copy. The bill is written to whoever owned the parcel at the start of the year, so it may carry the seller's name, and a missing bill leaves the debt in place.

faqs.q: Who hears a property tax appeal in Letcher County?
faqs.a: A local board of assessment appeals hears it in Whitesburg, after you have met with the PVA at 156 Main Street, Suite 105 and filed with the clerk. The filing deadline is the workday after the thirteen-day roll inspection ends.

faqs.q: Who pays the year's tax when a Letcher County house changes hands?
faqs.a: The settlement statement decides. The sheriff bills the January 1 owner, and sellers commonly credit the buyer for their months of ownership. Delinquent amounts are a lien that has to be cleared for the title to pass clean.
